about.title: Torrance Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A wet aisle inside a store off Hawthorne Boulevard. A cracked walkway outside an apartment complex near Crenshaw Boulevard. An unlit stairwell in a parking structure along Pacific Coast Highway. Falls like these happen quietly in Torrance every week, and the people who get hurt often blame themselves first. Under California law, the question is not whether you were careful enough. It is whether the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and did nothing to fix it or warn you. That element, called notice, is where most Torrance premises cases are won or lost. Evidence disappears fast: spills get mopped, surveillance systems overwrite footage in days, and incident reports get filed away. You generally have two years to file, but that window shrinks considerably if the property belongs to the City of Torrance, Los Angeles County, or another public entity. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Torrance Residents Start With LawProactive

items.title: Notice is the whole case, so we move quickly
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorney you are matched with can send preservation letters for surveillance video and maintenance logs before they are erased or lost.

items.title: Deadlines that vary by who owns the property
items.desc: Most Torrance premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but claims against a city, county, or school district must be presented on a much shorter clock. An early conversation helps you avoid missing either one.

items.title: Being partly at fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than eliminated. If you were texting or wearing slick shoes, you may still have a claim worth pursuing.

items.question: I fell in a store parking lot on Hawthorne Boulevard and didn't report it. Is it too late?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Torrance's commercial corridors are lined with businesses that keep camera footage, but many systems overwrite within a week or two, so speed matters more than a formal report. Write down exactly where you fell, photograph the spot as soon as you can, and note any witnesses. An attorney can then request footage and records before they vanish.

items.question: What if the fall happened on a City of Torrance sidewalk or in a county building?
items.answer: Claims against public entities in California follow different rules than claims against private owners. You typically must file a written government claim within six months of the injury, well before the usual two-year deadline. Missing that step can bar the case entirely, which is why we encourage you to reach out early even if you are unsure who owns the property.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle premises liability cases on a contingency basis, which means they are paid only if there is a recovery. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
